body.statement: Fix a canonical residual kernel \(q_{\mathrm{can}}(x\mid c,h)\). It generates the unique coupling \(\gamma_{\mathrm{can},cx}=p_cq_{\mathrm{can}}(x\mid c,h)\), and therefore spans \(\Gamma(p,r)\) if and only if \(\Gamma(p,r)=\{\gamma_{\mathrm{can}}\}\). With positive margins and \(|\mathcal C|\ge2\) and \(|\mathcal X|\ge2\), \(\operatorname{dim}\Gamma(p,r)=(|\mathcal C|-1)(|\mathcal X|-1)>0\), so no single fixed canonical residual law realizes the free-selector envelope. The family in \(\mathrm{lem:projected\text{-}construction}\) satisfies Definition 6 selector by selector and makes no common Equation-11 Layer-3-map claim.
body.justification: This supporting proposition records the exact quantifier boundary between a fixed canonical residual law and a free selector family.
body.gap: The canonical Equation-11 construction determines one residual conditional law, not an entire positive-dimensional transportation polytope.
body.consumer: An abstraction user can verify whether selector-specific residual distributions are admissible for the intended analysis.
